public_rationale: The searched records do not settle whether original Imagen had usable competence with weight, mass or density. General image benchmarks and failures on a horse–astronaut prompt do not establish the claimed absence of all such competence. No controlled evaluation of these concepts in the original model was located.
limitations: The behavioral interpretation makes the claim testable but does not settle philosophical questions about understanding.
Missing evaluations are not evidence that the model lacked the concepts.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Imagen has no understanding of weight, mass or density.

statement.excerpt: (In reality, Imagen has no idea what weight, mass, or density are.)

our_interpretation: The target is the original Imagen system discussed in May 2022, not later Imagen versions.
For this ongoing state, the target period is May 2022 through publication, the period of the model’s initial public report.
The ordinary behavioral reading is that Imagen lacks systematic usable competence with these physical concepts.
This does not require deciding whether a machine has subjective understanding. Neither a single implausible image nor the architecture alone establishes absence of competence.
criteria.support_condition: Controlled evaluations of the original model consistently fail to demonstrate usable knowledge of weight, mass and density across varied prompts, after accounting for general image-generation and language-following errors.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Controlled evaluations demonstrate systematic, transferable competence with one or more of these concepts, contradicting the blanket assertion of no understanding.

evidence.publisher: Google Research authors, published through arXiv
evidence.explanation: The original report describes a text-to-image evaluation framework. The inspected evaluation does not establish either systematic competence or its absence for weight, mass and density.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Controlled tests of the preserved original model across weight, mass and density relationships, with matched language and rendering controls and independently scored outputs.
